jobs.title: Executive Director - myPlace Health PACE
jobs.description:
myPlace Health is built around a simple but powerful belief: older adults deserve the support they need to live safely, independently, and with dignity in their own communities. As a PACE (Program of All Inclusive Care for the Elderly) organization backed by SCAN Group, myPlace Health brings together customized medical care, social activities, and daily support for participants and their families – all under one roof.

Our centers are more than healthcare facilities. They are vibrant community hubs where participants are known by name, valued, and supported as whole people. Behind that experience is a dedicated, interdisciplinary team working together to coordinate care, remove barriers, and improve quality of life for some of the most medically and socially complex populations.

For employees, myPlace Health offers the opportunity to do deeply meaningful work in a highly collaborative setting. Team members are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas, and grow alongside a mission that prioritizes compassion, respect, and impact. The result is a culture where people feel connected—to their colleagues, their participants, and the communities they serve.

At myPlace Health, work is more than a job. It’s a shared commitment to honoring what matters most.

As a PACE (Program of All Inclusive Care for the Elderly) organization backed by SCAN Group, myPlace Health brings together customized medical care, social activities, and daily support for participants and their families – all under one roof.

Our centers are more than healthcare facilities. They are vibrant community hubs where participants are known by name, valued, and supported as whole people. Behind that experience is a dedicated, interdisciplinary team working together to coordinate care, remove barriers, and improve quality of life for some of the most medically and socially complex populations.

For employees, myPlace Health offers the opportunity to do deeply meaningful work in a highly collaborative setting. Team members are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas, and grow alongside a mission that prioritizes compassion, respect, and impact. The result is a culture where people feel connected—to their colleagues, their participants, and the communities they serve.

At myPlace Health, work is more than a job. It’s a shared commitment to honoring what matters most.

About SCAN

SCAN Group is a not-for-profit organization dedicated to tackling the most pressing issues facing older adults in the United States. SCAN Group is the sole corporate member of SCAN Health Plan, one of the nation’s leading not-for-profit Medicare Advantage plans, serving more than 300,000 members in California, Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Washington and Texas. SCAN has been a mission-driven organization dedicated to keeping seniors healthy and independent for more than 40 years and is known throughout the healthcare industry and nationally as a leading expert in senior healthcare. SCAN employees are a group of talented, passionate professionals who are committed to supporting older adults on their aging journey, while also innovating healthcare for seniors everywhere. Employees are provided in-depth training and access to state-of-the-art tools necessary to do their jobs, as well as development and growth opportunities. SCAN takes great pride in recognizing our team members as experts in their fields and rewarding them for their efforts. If you are interested in becoming part of an organization that is innovating senior healthcare visit www.thescangroup.org, www.scanhealthplan.com, or follow us on LinkedIn; Facebook; and Twitter.

About MyPlace Health

myPlace Health was founded in 2021 by mission-driven healthcare leaders and organizations that are committed to drastically improving health outcomes, quality and experience for vulnerable older adults and frail seniors. We are an integrated care delivery organization that specializes in providing personalized care and coverage to older adults who wish to remain safely living in their homes and communities for as long as possible, rather than living in a nursing facility.

Our mission is simple: to enable seniors to live the independent lives they deserve. The primary ways in which we pursue our mission are through capitated arrangements with government payers, such as Medicare and Medicaid under the PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) model, and as a value-based provider working in partnership with local health plans.

We are building a mission-driven team that shares our passion for redefining the way older adults experience care as they “age in place” in the community. This is a unique opportunity to take on one of our country’s most challenging healthcare problems and it is a unique moment in time to join us as we scale up to spread our mission across markets.

The Job

The Executive Director is responsible for serving as the senior operating leader for an assigned market, with full accountability for strategy, operations, culture, growth, participant experience, regulatory compliance, and financial performance. In close partnership with the Executive Medical Director, local leaders, and national leadership teams, this role drives the successful execution of the care model to achieve key clinical, quality, member experience, and business outcomes. The Executive Director leads and develops a high-performing market team, builds strong relationships with community and regulatory partners, and ensures the market operates in alignment with organizational goals and PACE requirements. This role is designed for a mission-driven, seasoned operating leader who brings experience leading integrated care operations, ideally in PACE or similar value-based care environments, and who is passionate about improving how care is delivered to vulnerable older adults while helping build capabilities that can scale across markets.

You Will

Serve as the executive operating leader for the market with full accountability for strategy, planning, operations, participant experience, compliance, and overall performance outcomes.

Partner with local and national clinical and operational leadership to drive high-quality care, strong clinical outcomes, participant satisfaction, operational excellence, and regulatory compliance.

Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing, diverse market team, including clinical and operational leaders, to support excellent care delivery and sustainable market success.

Establish, communicate, and model a clear operating strategy and culture vision that promotes accountability, engagement, service excellence, and alignment with organizational goals.

Collaborate with national leadership to implement, optimize, and sustain the infrastructure, systems, and operational processes needed to support all aspects of market performance.

Serve as the local expert in the care model and PACE regulatory requirements, ensuring the market maintains compliance and implements effective operational solutions to meet regulatory and organizational standards.

Oversee market financial performance, including budget development, resource planning, and ongoing monitoring of financial and operational results.

Represent the organization externally by building and maintaining effective relationships with providers, strategic partners, community-based organizations, and regulatory stakeholders.

Identify and advance opportunities to strengthen and adapt the care model to meet local community needs, improve participant outcomes, and leverage strategic partnerships.

Foster a culture of continuous learning, improvement, and operational ownership by leading with flexibility, sound judgment, and a service-oriented approach that supports participants, caregivers, and staff.

We seek Rebels who are curious about AI and its power to transform how we operate and serve our members.

Actively support the achievement of SCAN’s Vision and Goals.

Other duties as assigned.

Your Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Public Health, Gerontology, or a related field required

Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, care delivery, or related business leadership roles

Minimum of 7 years of supervisory, managerial or executive leadership experience

Passion for serving high-risk, vulnerable, and frail older adults

Leadership experience building, scaling, growing, improving, and/or turning around care delivery businesses or clinical business units

Demonstrated understanding of or experience leading care management functions within PACE, Medicaid managed care, Medicare Advantage, or other government-sponsored health plan models

Proven ability to inspire, lead, coach, and mentor high-performing teams in a way that reinforces organizational culture and values

Strong ability to communicate confidently and persuasively with internal audiences

What's in it for you?

Base Pay Range: $150,000-$200,000, Salary + Bonus Opportunity
Work Mode: Onsite
An annual employee bonus program
Medical, Dental, Vision Coverage
Generous paid-time-off (PTO)
11 paid holidays per year, plus 1 additional floating holiday
Excellent 401(k) Retirement Saving Plan with employer match
Robust employee recognition program
Robust Wellness Program
Tuition reimbursement
An opportunity to become part of a team that makes a difference to our members and our community every day!

We're always looking for talented people to join our team! Qualified applicants are encouraged to apply now!

Transform your career with a job that makes a difference in people’s lives!

myPlace Health is building a mission-driven team that shares our passion for redefining the way older adults experience care as they “age in place” in the community. This is a unique opportunity to take on one of our country’s most challenging healthcare problems and join a fast-growing, dynamic team as we prepare to scale our mission to serve more markets.

Learn more about open career opportunities at myPlace Health and to find out how you can join an industry-leading team of clinicians, operators, technologists, and healthcare industry subject matter experts.

If you want to be part of a team committed to drastically improving health outcomes and quality of life for older adults and frail seniors, we want to hear from you!

This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic thinker and skilled fundraiser who is equally comfortable building a long-term development plan, sitting down with a donor, crafting a compelling message, and bringing a successful fundraising event to life.

Kids FIRST is an Accredited Children's Advocacy Center that has served Lane County since 1994. Our multidisciplinary team provides coordinated, compassionate services to children and families affected by abuse and crime. Grounded in integrity, growth, and resilience, Kids FIRST has been consistently recognized as one of Oregon's 100 Best Nonprofits to Work For.

Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, leadership team, and community partners, the Development Director will:
Create and lead fundraising strategies, budgets, revenue forecasts, and goals.
Grow annual giving, major gifts, grants, sponsorships, planned giving, and corporate and foundation partnerships.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward donors through authentic, long-term relationships.
Lead fundraising events from initial vision through execution and evaluation.
Guide donor communications, marketing, storytelling, social media, and public relations.
Represent Kids FIRST at donor meetings, community events, networking opportunities, and speaking engagements.
Lead and support development staff, volunteers, interns, and consultants.

Qualifications

Our ideal candidate brings at least two years of professional fundraising experience and a record of building donor relationships, making compelling solicitations, and securing gifts. They are an engaging communicator and confident relationship-builder with strong strategic planning, project management, budgeting, and organizational skills. A bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience is required. Bilingual English/Spanish skills are preferred.

Benefits

Kids FIRST offers 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families; a 3% retirement match; 13 paid holidays; generous PTO and separate sick leave; Summer Fridays; a weekly self-care hour; $1,200 Mental Health HRA; FireMed membership; and a sabbatical opportunity after five years.

Some local travel and occasional evening or weekend availability are required.

To be considered, applicants must submit both a resume and cover letter.

new_jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer - Rare Earth - Critical Minerals
new_jobs.description:
Chief Executive Officer – Rare Earths / Critical Minerals

Public Markets | Project Development | Strategic Capital

Confidential Executive Search | Nasdaq-Listed Critical Minerals Company

Location:
Remote – U.S. based,
Travel:
Significant travel to SOUTHWEST USA, Washington, D.C. and capital-market/strategic partner meetings
Industry:
Rare Earth Elements / Critical Minerals / Mining & Mineral Processing
Company Overview

Our client is a publicly traded U.S.-focused rare earth elements and critical minerals company advancing a strategically important development and mineral-processing platform in West Texas.
The company is entering an important stage of growth following its entry into the U.S. public markets and requires an experienced Chief Executive Officer capable of leading the organization through project development, financing, commercialization and long-term value creation.
Position Overview

The Chief Executive Officer will provide overall strategic, financial and organizational leadership for the company.
This is a conventional CEO mandate
requiring C-suite leadership, public-company sophistication, capital-markets credibility and the ability to advance a major U.S. critical-minerals project from development toward commercial operation.
A particularly important requirement is a deep network in Washington, D.C.
and demonstrated ability to engage senior government, agency and industry stakeholders around critical minerals, national security and domestic supply-chain development.
The CEO will work closely with the Board, technical leadership, investment banks, commercial banks, investors, strategic partners and government stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities

Corporate Leadership

Lead overall corporate strategy, execution and organizational development.
Work closely with the Board to establish strategic priorities, capital requirements and measurable development milestones.
Build and lead the executive and operating organization required to advance the company through its next stage of development.
Establish accountability across technical, financial, regulatory and commercial functions.

Project Development & Operations

Provide executive oversight of the West Texas project and its development toward commercial production.
Work with technical leadership across geology, metallurgy, processing, engineering, permitting and project development.
Understand project economics, CAPEX/OPEX, schedules, technical risk and financing requirements.
Maintain regular presence at the West Texas / Greater El Paso operation.

Direct technical mining management is not the primary function of the CEO; however, mining, critical-minerals or comparable natural-resource development experience is strongly preferred.

Capital Markets

Serve as a credible public-market representative of the company.
Develop relationships with institutional investors, analysts, investment banks, commercial banks and strategic investors.
Lead equity, debt and project-financing strategy in conjunction with the Board and CFO.
Clearly communicate project economics, development milestones, capital requirements, risks and strategic value.
Participate actively in investor presentations, conferences, financings and other public-company activities.

Washington / Government Strategy

Utilize established senior-level relationships within Washington, D.C. to advance the company's strategic objectives.
Develop productive relationships across relevant federal agencies, government programs, Congressional stakeholders and national-security organizations.
Identify and pursue appropriate grants, loans, loan guarantees, strategic investments and other forms of non-dilutive or government-supported capital.
Coordinate government funding opportunities with the company's overall commercial banking, project-finance and capital-markets strategy.
Position the company's U.S. rare-earth platform within national priorities involving critical minerals, defense, advanced manufacturing and domestic supply-chain security.

Strategic Partnerships

Develop relationships with major industrial, defense, technology and manufacturing organizations.
Pursue strategic partnerships, offtake agreements, government-supported initiatives and potential downstream relationships.
Evaluate acquisitions, joint ventures and other strategic opportunities that could expand the company's U.S. critical-minerals platform.

Ideal Background

Prior CEO, President, COO or comparable C-suite leadership experience
.
Demonstrated experience leading a growth-stage, project-development or public company.
Strong understanding of U.S. capital markets and corporate finance
.
Experience working with investment banks, commercial banks, institutional investors and Boards.
Significant established relationships in Washington, D.C.

Demonstrated understanding of federal funding, government programs and strategic financing.
Mining, rare earths, critical minerals or natural-resource development experience strongly preferred.
Ability to understand and communicate complex technical projects without needing to personally serve as the company's chief technical officer.
Experience with major capital projects, project financing, infrastructure or industrial development.
Strong public-company communication and investor credibility.
Comfortable operating in an entrepreneurial environment with significant personal accountability.

REM Community Services,
a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.

Program Director, IDD Services

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.

Manage the day-to-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.
Manage program staff members including performance evaluations, scheduling, and orientation.
Make recommendations and/or decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, corrective action, and terminations.
Manage the implementation of program planning; monitor delivery of services and supports; ensure services are consistent, engaging, and relevant to the individuals served.
Must be available on-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
An equivalent combination of education and experience.
Other education, experience, training, licensure, or certification per state requirements or as required by applicable regulations.
Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi-task to meet deadlines.
Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.

Why Join Us?

Full, Part-time, and As Needed schedules available.

401(k) with company match.
Paid time off and holiday pay.
Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
